Queer Theology
kweer THEE-uh-luh-jee
noun phrase (academic framework)
Academic theological subfield originating in the late 1980s and early 1990s, applying queer theory (Butler, Sedgwick, Foucault) to biblical and theological texts. The term "queer" in the academic sense includes deliberate destabilization of binary categories, not just gay-and-lesbian identity politics.

📖 Biblical Definition

Queer theology is the academic theological subfield that applies queer theory — a 1990s Butler / Sedgwick / Foucault framework that deliberately destabilizes binary categories (male / female, heterosexual / homosexual, normal / deviant) — to biblical interpretation and Christian theology. It is distinct from (and more radical than) affirming theology. Major representatives: Marcella Althaus-Reid (Indecent Theology, 2000), Patrick Cheng (Radical Love, 2011), Robert Goss, Linn Marie Tonstad. Where affirming theology argues that committed-monogamous same-sex unions can fit within the existing biblical framework, queer theology argues that the framework itself is the problem — that the creational binaries of Gen 1:27 are oppressive social constructions that the gospel destabilizes, that Jesus himself is queer (Cheng's central claim), that the church should embrace fluidity over fixity in every category from gender to family to theology. From the Reformed-confessional standpoint, queer theology is rebutted at the foundation: Gen 1:27 establishes the male-female creational binary as the imago Dei structure of humanity; Christ's incarnation as the male Son of Mary (Matt 1:25; Luke 1:31; Luke 2:21) consecrates rather than destabilizes biological sex; and the apostolic Lord's words at Matt 19:4-6 ground all sexual ethics in the creational binary. The dictionary holds the historic Christian position categorically. # voice-lock-ok: progressive: this entry names and rebuts queer theology.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Academic theological subfield (since late 1980s) applying queer theory to biblical interpretation; more radical than affirming theology in that it rejects the underlying biblical framework rather than reinterpreting it; representatives Althaus-Reid, Cheng, Goss, Tonstad; rebutted from Gen 1:27 + Matt 19:4-6.

QUEER THEOLOGY, noun phrase. Academic theological subfield since late 1980s applying queer theory to biblical and theological texts.

Major representatives: Marcella Althaus-Reid (Argentine; Indecent Theology, 2000); Patrick Cheng (Asian-American; Radical Love, 2011); Robert Goss; Linn Marie Tonstad.

Distinct from affirming theology: more radical, rejects the creational male-female binary itself rather than reinterpreting biblical sexuality passages within it.

Rebutted at Gen 1:27 (creational binary), Matt 19:4-6 (Christ's affirmation of creational binary), and the apostolic ethic generally.

📖 Key Scripture

Genesis 1:27 — "So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them."

Matthew 19:4-6 — "And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder."

Luke 2:21 — "And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb."

1 Corinthians 6:11 — "And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Queer theology is itself a corruption pattern that the dictionary names and rebuts. It is more radical than affirming theology in that it rejects the creational binary rather than reinterpreting biblical sexuality within it.

expand to see more

Destabilizing the creational binary. Queer theology's defining move is to treat the male-female binary of Gen 1:27 as itself an oppressive social construct rather than as the imago Dei structure of humanity. The plain reading of Gen 1:27, reinforced by Christ's appeal to it at Matt 19:4-6, rebuts the framing: the male-female binary is given, embodied, image-of-God, and creational, not contingent or culturally constructed. The Lord's appeal to Genesis to settle the divorce question is the apostolic-canonical pattern for settling any sexuality question. # voice-lock-ok: progressive: this paragraph rebuts queer theology's destabilization of the creational binary.

Christ as queer. Patrick Cheng's Radical Love proposes that Christ himself is queer because Christ destabilizes categories (Jew / Gentile, slave / free, male / female) per Gal 3:28. The proposal collapses two distinct claims: (a) Christ relativizes some social categories with respect to salvation (Jew/Gentile, slave/free; Gal 3:28's pre-resurrection list); (b) Christ destabilizes the creational male-female binary (Cheng's queer claim). The Reformed reader: the gospel relativizes the social categories of position; it does not relativize the creational categories of sex. Gal 3:28's 'neither male nor female' addresses the position-before-God of those in Christ, not the embodied creational structure of humanity (Eph 5:22-33 written by the same apostle explicitly maintains the husband-wife, male-female structure within the gospel).

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Academic subfield applying queer theory to theology since late 1980s; major representatives Althaus-Reid, Cheng, Goss, Tonstad; more radical than affirming theology; rebutted from Gen 1:27 + Matt 19:4-6.

Academic origin: late 1980s and early 1990s, applying queer theory (Judith Butler, Eve Sedgwick, Michel Foucault) to theology

Distinct from gay-and-lesbian theology of the 1970s-80s: more radical, anti-binary, anti-essentialist

Major works: Marcella Althaus-Reid, Indecent Theology (2000); Patrick Cheng, Radical Love (2011); Linn Marie Tonstad, God and Difference (2016)

Reformed-confessional rebuttals operate at the foundation: Gen 1:27 creational binary; Matt 19:4-6 Christ's appeal to it; Eph 5 husband-wife structure maintained in the gospel
